scope_note: The emergency and oral prescription pair, repaired after the V7 round and re-sealed. The repair teaches that a Massachusetts pharmacist must satisfy both sovereigns' emergency definitions, names all three items the follow-up prescription carries on its face, and corrects the consequence of a Failover that fails its conditions. A later editor answered the scope-gate signals both sections carried once a parallel repair's rules landed: it added the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(a) record particulars to SG-CII-EMERGENCY-ORAL and declined the rest with reasons. Declined for SG-CII-EMERGENCY-ORAL: the two Failover rules, because a Failover is by definition a Schedule VI electronic prescription and the outage/Failover distinction is SG-MA-ORAL-PRESCRIPTIONS' declared objective; MA-RX-FORMAT-CONTENT and MA-RX-REQUIRED-ELEMENTS, because on this pathway the content list is fixed by 105 CMR 721.060(B)(2)'s cross-reference to s. 20(a) and by 21 CFR 1306.05, both taught; and MA-CII-OPIOID-PARTIAL-FILL-NOTATION, whose subject is SG-CII-LIFECYCLE's. Declined for SG-MA-ORAL-PRESCRIPTIONS: the same three, the section already quoting the s. 20(a) element list in full.

prior_audit_reference.note: V7B rated the superseded SG-CII-EMERGENCY-ORAL hash MINOR_EDIT and CLAUDE-FRESH-B4-SG-V7C rated the superseded SG-MA-ORAL-PRESCRIPTIONS hash MINOR_EDIT. Both drove this repair, bind none of the hashes frozen here, and are excluded from the auditor package.
